title: 1999 AHSME Problem 24
statement: Six points on a circle are given. Four of the chords joining pairs of the six points are selected at random. What is the probability that the four chords form a convex quadrilateral?

solutions.text:
There are \(\binom{6}{2} = 15\) chords, so \(\binom{15}{4} = 1365\) ways to select four of them. A convex quadrilateral arises exactly when the four chords are the sides of a quadrilateral on four of the six points, and each choice of \(4\) points gives exactly one such quadrilateral.

Hence there are \(\binom{6}{4} = 15\) favorable outcomes, and the probability is \(\dfrac{15}{1365} = \dfrac{1}{91}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
